bottlenecks.description: Molecular docking conformational search space grows combinatorially with ligand flexibility, interaction motifs, and binding-site geometry, making exhaustive evaluation intractable for large flexible molecules
bottlenecks.evidence: Agu et al. 2023; arxiv.org/abs/2508.18147 — 'The number of candidate poses grows combinatorially with ligand flexibility, interaction motifs and binding-site geometry, making exhaustive evaluation inefficient'

bottlenecks.description: Physics-based virtual screening of billion-compound libraries is computationally prohibitive: brute-force docking of 36B compounds would require ~3.6×10^8 CPU-hours (~$3.6M cloud cost, ~130 years on 320 cores)
bottlenecks.evidence: V-SYNTHES2, Nature Communications 2025 (PMC13332051) — 'brute-force docking of 36 billion compounds would require ~3.6×10^8 CPU-hours'

bottlenecks.description: AlphaFold-style structure prediction scales cubically with sequence length due to triangle attention in the Pairformer backbone; Boltz-1 requires >15 min for a single 2048-token sequence on A100 GPU
bottlenecks.evidence: Pairmixer (arxiv.org/html/2510.18870v2) — 'Boltz-1 requires over 15 minutes to process a single 2048-token sequence on an A100 GPU'; 'triangle attention requires attention operations, introducing substantial memory and runtime overhead'

bottlenecks.description: ADMET prediction remains a critical bottleneck: ~40% of preclinical candidate drugs fail due to insufficient ADMET profiles, and nearly 30% of marketed drugs are withdrawn due to unforeseen toxic reactions
bottlenecks.evidence: PMC12499773 — '~40% of preclinical candidate drugs fail due to insufficient ADMET profiles, while nearly 30% of marketed drugs are withdrawn due to unforeseen toxic reactions'

bottlenecks.description: Deep learning docking methods exhibit poor generalization to novel protein binding pockets, with regression models often failing to produce physically valid poses and most DL methods showing high steric tolerance
bottlenecks.evidence: RSC Chem. Sci. 2025 (d5sc05395a) — 'significant challenges in generalization, particularly when encountering novel protein binding pockets'; 'regression models often fail to produce physically valid poses'

bottlenecks.description: Clinical trial failure rates remain ~90% from Phase 1 to BLA; AI-discovered drugs show 80-90% Phase I success but only ~40% Phase II success, comparable to historic averages
bottlenecks.evidence: Jayatunga et al. Drug Discov. Today 2024 (doi:10.1016/j.drudis.2024.104009) — 'In Phase II the success rate is ~40%'; npj Drug Discovery 2025 — 'nearly 95% failure rate between Phase 1 and BLA'

bottlenecks.description: Molecular dynamics simulations for binding free energy calculations are extremely expensive: FEP+ requires ~128.8 perturbations/day per DGX A100 system, limiting throughput in lead optimization
bottlenecks.evidence: NVIDIA DGX Infrastructure Solution for Drug Discovery (WP-11016-001) — 'BACE-1 simulations have a maximum throughput of 128.8 perturbations/day per DGX'

np_hard_problems.problem: Molecular Docking (Maximum Weighted Independent Set / Maximum Vertex-Weighted Clique)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — mapping pharmacophore interactions to graph vertices and finding the optimal compatible subset is provably intractable for large densely connected graphs
current_approaches: Force-field-based stochastic search (AutoDock Vina, Glide SP)
Graph-based combinatorial optimization mapping to MWIS/MVWCP
Quantum annealing on neutral-atom QPUs (Rydberg blockade)
Deep learning pose prediction (diffusion models, regression architectures)
gaps: Size mismatch between biologically relevant systems and NISQ quantum hardware capacity
Heuristic search provides no optimality guarantees
Scoring functions lack accuracy for entropy and induced-fit effects
DL methods show poor generalization to novel binding pockets

np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — selecting one rotamer per residue from a discrete library to minimize total pairwise-decomposable conformational energy is provably intractable (Pierce & Winfree, 2002)
current_approaches: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) with QUBO encoding
gaps: AlphaFold2 sidechain positioning deviates from experimental data by up to 20%
Rosetta packer is heuristic with no global optimality guarantee
QAOA shot scaling remains below classical exhaustive search rates at moderate flexibility
Classical preprocessing does not significantly reduce low-energy basins

np_hard_problems.problem: Protein Structure Alignment (Optimal RMSD under Correspondence)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — reducible to the largest common point set (LCP) problem or 3D substructure isomorphism, both proven NP-complete (Goldman et al., 1999)
gaps: Exhaustive search is O(n!·m!) for proteins of length n, m
Continuous 6-DOF search space cannot be discretely sampled without missing global optimum
Scoring functions are non-convex with many local minima
Flexible alignment with rotamers is NP-complete to NP-hard

np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-complete for detailed models (Lathrop, 1994) — aligning sequence to structural template with pairwise interactions is intractable
gaps: Energy function accuracy degrades with sequence length

np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard — even simplified models with both ligand and receptor flexibility are intractable (Fraenkel, 1993)
gaps: Induced-fit effects poorly captured by rigid-receptor approximations
No polynomial-time algorithm exists for guaranteed optimal solution

sota_approaches.name: AlphaFold3
sota_approaches.description: Diffusion-based biomolecular structure prediction modeling protein-ligand, protein-nucleic acid, and protein-protein interactions with atomic accuracy; transforms structure-based drug design

sota_approaches.name: Boltz-1 / Boltz-2
sota_approaches.description: Open-source biomolecular structure prediction foundation model achieving AlphaFold3-competitive accuracy; Boltz-2 ranks highest among ML-based binding affinity prediction tools in benchmarks
sota_approaches.citation: Wohlwend et al., 2024; benchmarked in arxiv.org/abs/2605.04265 — 'Boltz-2 and DrugFormDTA ranked highest overall among ML-based approaches'

sota_approaches.name: TerraBind
sota_approaches.description: Foundation model for protein-ligand structure and binding affinity prediction using coarse pocket-level representation (Cβ + heavy atoms only); 26× faster inference than SOTA with ~20% improved affinity accuracy
sota_approaches.citation: arxiv.org/abs/2602.07735 — '26-fold faster inference than state-of-the-art methods while improving affinity prediction accuracy by ~20%'

sota_approaches.name: RosettaVS / OpenVS
sota_approaches.description: AI-accelerated physics-based virtual screening platform with active learning triage; screened 5.5B Enamine-REAL library in <7 days on 3000 CPUs + 1 RTX2080 GPU, discovering single-digit µM binders
sota_approaches.citation: Nature Communications 15, 2024 (doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52061-7) — 'Screening in both cases is completed in less than seven days'

sota_approaches.name: V-SYNTHES2
sota_approaches.description: Structure-based virtual screening of 36B Enamine REAL Space using iterative modular algorithm with CapSelect; scales linearly with synthons rather than total compounds, achieving >10,000-fold computational reduction
sota_approaches.citation: Nature Communications 2025 (PMC13332051) — 'V-SYNTHES2 reduces the required docking to ≈3.8 million compounds (~38,400 CPU-hours; ≈$380)'

sota_approaches.name: Pairmixer
sota_approaches.description: Streamlined alternative to AlphaFold3 Pairformer backbone eliminating triangle attention while preserving geometric reasoning; matches SOTA accuracy with 34% fewer training GPU-days and up to 4× faster inference on long sequences
sota_approaches.citation: arxiv.org/html/2510.18870v2 — 'Pairmixer consistently matches the performance of Pairformer backbone while training in 34% fewer GPU-days'

sota_approaches.name: SWDOCKP2
sota_approaches.description: Performance-portable virtual screening framework achieving 1.9 trillion ligand-receptor pairs daily on Sunway OceanLight supercomputer (39M cores) — 10× faster than prior SOTA
sota_approaches.citation: ACM SC25 (doi:10.1145/3712285.3759833) — '1.9 trillion ligand-receptor pairs daily across eight targets... 10× faster than prior state-of-the-art'

sota_approaches.name: Diffusion-based Docking (FlowDock, etc.)
sota_approaches.description: Generative diffusion models for molecular docking pose prediction achieving superior pose accuracy over traditional methods, though with challenges in physical plausibility and steric tolerance
sota_approaches.citation: RSC Chem. Sci. 2025 (d5sc05395a) — 'generative diffusion models achieve superior pose accuracy, while hybrid methods offer the best balance'

failure_modes.mode: ADMET attrition: ~40% of preclinical candidates fail due to poor pharmacokinetics or toxicity, often discovered late in development
failure_modes.mitigation: Early integration of ML-based ADMET prediction (GNNs, multitask models) in hit-to-lead optimization; use of self-supervised pretraining on large compound datasets (HelixADMET)

failure_modes.mode: Clinical trial failure: ~90% failure rate from Phase 1 to BLA; AI-discovered drugs show ~40% Phase II success (proof-of-concept), comparable to traditional drugs
failure_modes.mitigation: Focus on validated targets with clinical evidence; improve disease modeling and biomarker stratification; AI-driven clinical trial optimization

failure_modes.mode: DL docking generalization failure: deep learning docking methods perform poorly on novel protein binding pockets not represented in training data
failure_modes.mitigation: Hybrid physics-ML approaches; ensemble docking with receptor flexibility; active learning to iteratively expand training coverage

failure_modes.mode: Scoring function inaccuracy: empirical and force-field scoring functions fail to capture entropy, induced-fit, and solvent effects, leading to false positives/negatives
failure_modes.mitigation: Free energy perturbation (FEP+) calculations for lead optimization; MM-PBSA/GBSA rescoring; ML-based affinity prediction (Boltz-2, DrugFormDTA)

failure_modes.mode: AlphaFold hallucination in disordered regions: ~30-40% of residues have low pLDDT confidence; predictions fail for IDRs, ligand-bound states, and PTMs
failure_modes.mitigation: Orthogonal experimental validation (cryo-EM, X-ray); ensemble AF models; integration with MD simulations for dynamic refinement

failure_modes.mode: AI-designed drugs acting on established targets: most AI-discovered drugs target previously validated mechanisms, limiting therapeutic novelty
failure_modes.mitigation: Invest in novel target identification via multi-omics AI; combine generative design with target deconvolution; focus on underserved indications

hardware_requirements.minimum: Single NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU for AlphaFold inference and DL-based docking; 32-64 CPU cores for traditional docking; 128GB RAM for large library processing
hardware_requirements.recommended: NVIDIA DGX A100 (8×A100 80GB) or DGX H100 (8×H100 80GB) for structure prediction at scale; 3000+ CPU cluster with GPU acceleration for billion-compound virtual screening; NVLink/NVSwitch interconnect for multi-GPU training

scalability_limits.limit: Brute-force physics-based docking of full chemical libraries
scalability_limits.threshold: 36 billion compounds → ~3.6×10^8 CPU-hours (~$3.6M cloud, ~130 years on 320 cores); requires hierarchical/funnel approaches (V-SYNTHES2: >10,000× reduction)
2048 tokens → >15 min on A100 GPU (Boltz-1); Pairmixer reduces to ~250s but still O(n³) scaling with sequence length
96k atoms → 3,700 ns/day on 1 DGX A100; 150,000 ns/day on 10 DGX A100; FEP+ limited to ~128.8 perturbations/day per DGX
1.9 trillion ligand-receptor pairs/day on 39M-core Sunway OceanLight (SWDOCKP2); ~36s/compound on single CPU core for physics-based docking
540-node MWIS problem solved on neutral-atom QPU emulator; biologically relevant systems require divide-and-conquer decomposition due to limited qubit count
PDB contains ~200K experimental structures; novel binding pockets and underrepresented protein families limit generalization of learned scoring functions

regulations: FDA Draft Guidance (Jan 2025): 'Considerations for the Use of Artificial Intelligence to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products' — covers AI in nonclinical, clinical, postmarketing, and manufacturing phases
Executive Order 14110 on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of AI — 150 requirements including 8 for HHS
CDER AI Council established 2024 for oversight and coordination of AI in drug development
21 CFR Parts 50, 56, 812 — human subject protections and investigational device exemptions for AI clinical investigations
45 CFR Part 46 (Common Rule) — proposed amendments for AI and digital health research
Proposed FDA-led AI regulatory sandboxes for biopharmaceutical applications with multi-stakeholder governance
challenges: Model validation: lack of standardized benchmarks for AI/ML models in regulatory decision-making
Data quality and representativeness: training data biases leading to inequitable drug efficacy across populations
Explainability: black-box deep learning models (diffusion-based docking, structure prediction) lack interpretability for regulatory review
Intellectual property: AI-assisted invention patentability and inventorship criteria unclear (USPTO MPEP update needed)
Data privacy: patient data in AI-driven pharmacovigilance and real-world evidence requires HIPAA/GDPR compliance
Transparency: level of documentation required for AI model development, performance monitoring, and validation
Harmonization: global alignment of AI in drug discovery regulations across FDA, EMA, PMDA

cost_tradeoffs.cost: ~$0.01/CPU-hour; ~36s/compound on single core; $3.6M for 36B library brute-force
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Physically interpretable, no training data required, well-validated scoring functions

cost_tradeoffs.cost: ~$380 for 36B library (10,000× reduction); requires GPU cluster for active learning model
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Giga-scale screening feasible in 48h; maintains physics-based accuracy for final ranking

cost_tradeoffs.cost: High training cost (GPU-days); inference 26× faster than physics-based (TerraBind)
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Superior pose accuracy; bypasses expensive all-atom diffusion; enables large-scale screening

cost_tradeoffs.cost: ~128.8 perturbations/day per DGX A100; expensive but experimental accuracy
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Gold standard for lead optimization; reduces late-stage attrition from poor binding affinity

cost_tradeoffs.cost: NISQ hardware limited to ~500-node problems; requires divide-and-conquer decomposition
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Potential for provably optimal solutions on MWIS; natural physical analogue via Rydberg blockade

cost_tradeoffs.cost: >15 min per 2048-token sequence on A100; Pairmixer reduces to ~250s with 34% fewer training GPU-days
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Near-experimental accuracy without costly crystallography/cryo-EM; enables structure-based design for previously intractable targets
